question.prompt:
In triangle \(ABC,\) \(\angle ABC = 45^\circ.\) Point \(D\) is on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(2 \cdot BD = CD\) and \(\angle DAB = 15^\circ.\) Find \(\angle ACB.\)

[Figure 1](figures/2001_AMC_12_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The given \(15^\circ\) angle suggests creating another \(15^\circ\) angle at \(B\). Draw a ray inside \(\angle ABD\) making \(30^\circ\) with \(BD\), and let it meet \(AD\) at \(F\). Because \(\angle ABD=45^\circ\), this intersection lies strictly between \(A\) and \(D\), and
\[
\angle ABF=45^\circ-30^\circ=15^\circ.
\]
Also \(\angle BAF=\angle BAD=15^\circ\), so triangle \(ABF\) is isosceles and \(AF=BF\).

Now use the given length ratio. In triangle \(ABD\),
\[
\angle BDA=180^\circ-45^\circ-15^\circ=120^\circ.
\]
Thus triangle \(BDF\) has angles \(30^\circ,120^\circ,30^\circ\), giving \(BD=DF\).

Let \(E\) be the midpoint of \(DC\). Since \(DC=2BD\), we have \(DE=EC=BD=DF\). Moreover, \(\angle FDE=60^\circ\), because \(DB\) and \(DE\) are opposite rays. Triangle \(DEF\) therefore has two equal sides enclosing a \(60^\circ\) angle, so it is equilateral.

Consequently, \(\angle FEC=120^\circ\). Triangles \(BDF\) and \(CEF\) are congruent by side-angle-side: \(BD=CE\), \(DF=EF\), and their included angles are both \(120^\circ\). Hence \(BF=CF\), so \(AF=CF\).

Finally, \(EF=EC\) makes triangle \(FEC\) isosceles, with \(\angle EFC=30^\circ\). Therefore
\[
\angle DFC=60^\circ+30^\circ=90^\circ.
\]
Since \(FA\) and \(FD\) are opposite rays, \(\angle AFC=90^\circ\) as well. Triangle \(AFC\) is a right isosceles triangle, so \(\angle FAC=45^\circ\). It follows that
\[
\angle BAC=15^\circ+45^\circ=60^\circ,
\qquad
\angle ACB=180^\circ-45^\circ-60^\circ=\boxed{75^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice D.
solutions.title: Create matching isosceles triangles
